therapeutic_hypothesis.proposed_mechanism: amyloid beta clearance via monoclonal antibody binding
therapeutic_hypothesis.intended_biology: reduction of amyloid plaque burden and neuroinflammation
therapeutic_hypothesis.target_population: participants with prodromal to mild Alzheimer's disease
therapeutic_hypothesis.primary_endpoint: change from baseline to week 77 in CDR-SB scale score

results.target_engagement_evidence: plasma amyloid beta 40 increased from 0.415 ng/mL to 46.6 ng/mL; plasma amyloid beta 42 increased from 0.0331 ng/mL to 2.94 ng/mL
biomarker_changes: plasma amyloid beta 40 increased 112-fold from baseline to week 53
plasma amyloid beta 42 increased 89-fold from baseline to week 53
whole brain volume decline reduced by 0.56% vs placebo
hippocampal volume decline reduced by 0.36% vs placebo
safety_signals: similar overall AE rates between arms (73.5% crenezumab vs 73.1% placebo)
lower SAE rate in crenezumab arm (8.2% vs 10.6% placebo)

context.duration: 77 weeks treatment with follow-up to 117 weeks
context.investigator_commentary: This study was discontinued due to an interim analysis in the BN29552 study, which indicated that Crenezumab was unlikely to meet its primary endpoint.
